questions.scenario: It's Sunday evening and your friends are playing a massive game of Gully Cricket. What is your main vibe?

options.A: Running around like crazy, bowling the fastest deliveries, and diving on the rough road to stop the ball.
options.B: Keeping track of the exact run-rate required and arguing with the other team over whether it was a 'wide' or not.
options.C: Taking the bat from a younger kid to show them exactly how to hold it to hit a perfect 'helicopter shot'.
options.D: Deciding who gets to bat first, who will open the bowling, and setting the strict fielding positions for the team.

questions.scenario: You are watching a tense India vs Pakistan T20 match on TV with your family. What are you doing?

options.A: Jumping off the sofa screaming on every single boundary and doing push-ups during the ad breaks to burn off the nervous energy.
options.B: Opening ESPNcricinfo on your phone to check Virat's exact strike rate against left-arm spinners in the last 5 years.
options.C: Pausing and rewinding the TV to closely analyze if the bowler's front foot was over the line or if their wrist position was wrong.
options.D: Predicting exactly what field changes the Captain should make in the final over to trap the batsman under pressure.

questions.scenario: You are teaching your younger sibling how to ride a bicycle for the first time. How do you approach it?

options.A: Running behind the cycle, holding the seat for 2 kilometers until you are sweating, just to build their stamina and confidence.
options.B: Calculating the exact speed they need to maintain and explaining the physics of balancing so they logically understand it.
options.C: Adjusting their posture continuously, telling them to keep their back straight, elbows slightly bent, and looking forward, not down.
options.D: Giving them a massive, emotional motivational speech about 'facing fears' right before you let go of the seat.

questions.scenario: The School Annual Sports Day is coming up. Your class is participating in the 4x100m relay race. You...

options.A: Make your team do 50 warm-up stretches and run 5 extra laps before the actual practice even begins.
options.B: Use your phone's stopwatch to time everyone's sprints to see who improved by exactly 0.5 seconds since yesterday.
options.C: Focus entirely on showing the team how to smoothly pass the baton hand-to-hand without losing any running momentum.
options.D: Observe everyone under pressure and select the final 4 runners based on who has the strongest winning mindset.

questions.scenario: You are watching an inspiring sports movie like 'Dangal' or 'Chak De! India'. What grabs your attention the most?

options.A: Getting totally pumped by the extreme training montages (like running in the sand) and immediately wanting to go work out.
options.B: Trying to figure out the tournament points table and the opponent team's winning streak statistics.
options.C: Being mesmerized by the perfect 'dhobi-pachad' (wrestling move) or hockey drag-flick, appreciating the physical art of it.
options.D: Admiring the strict discipline, master strategies, and the powerful aura of the coach (like Kabir Khan or Mahavir Phogat).

questions.scenario: Your housing society is organizing a weekend Badminton tournament. What is your role?

options.A: Setting up the net, painting the court lines, and actively hitting warm-up shuttles with all the uncles and aunties.
options.B: Creating a perfect mathematical draw/bracket sheet so that the two strongest players don't meet until the final match.
options.C: Pointing out that Sharma Ji's backhand grip is slightly wrong, which is exactly why the shuttle keeps hitting the net.
options.D: Collecting the entry fees, buying the trophies, and acting as the main referee to resolve any on-court fights.

questions.scenario: Your school football team just lost a crucial match against your biggest rival school. How do you react?

options.A: Make the team run extra penalty laps the very next morning so they build better stamina to never get tired again.
options.B: Watch the recording of the match to list exactly how many passes were intercepted and which side of the field was weakest.
options.C: Realize the rival team used a very specific ball-spinning technique that your team needs to learn and practice immediately.
options.D: Give a powerful, emotional 'dressing room speech' to lift the team's spirit and unite them for the next year's revenge.

questions.scenario: You are playing a multiplayer battle royale game (like BGMI/Free Fire) with your school friends. What is your playstyle?

options.A: Being the highly energetic rusher, dodging bullets, pushing into houses, and keeping the squad active and moving.
options.B: Memorizing the map, noting enemy drop locations, and calculating safe zone shrinking times perfectly.
options.C: Telling your friend to adjust their screen sensitivity and finger placement to improve their headshot aim.
options.D: Acting as the In-Game Leader (IGL), taking the final call on whether the squad should attack now or hide and wait.

questions.scenario: The PT Teacher is absent, and it's announced as a 'Free Period'. The class is chaotic. You...

options.A: Immediately grab the school football, run to the ground, and start an intense, sweaty match in the blazing sun.
options.B: Keep a mental tally of the scores, fouls, and exactly who is trying to cheat in the background.
options.C: Show your friends a cool new football trick or a 'rainbow flick' you learned by watching Instagram reels.
options.D: Take charge, silence the class, split them into two perfectly fair teams, and act as the official umpire.

questions.scenario: You are trying to master a brand new physical skill, like skating, swimming, or dancing. How do you learn best?

options.A: Sweating it out, falling down 20 times, getting a few bruises, and trying again and again until your legs hurt.
options.B: Watching 5 different YouTube tutorials to understand the fundamental rules, common mistakes, and progression steps.
options.C: Recording yourself on your phone and watching it back in slow-motion to correct your footwork and posture precisely.
options.D: Setting a strict 1-month goal, planning a daily practice schedule, and mentally pushing yourself not to quit.

Role_1.title: Field Drill Coach / Fitness Trainer
Role_1.primary_match_text: You are pure energy! You believe that sweat, stamina, and hard work beat talent any day. You love being on the ground, pushing physical limits, and staying active.
Role_1.day_in_the_life: Running on the field with athletes, designing intense gym workouts, throwing hundreds of practice balls, and pushing players to become the fittest version of themselves.
Role_1.alternative_match_text: Your high-energy and active lifestyle make you a perfect fit for a Physiotherapist, Gym Owner, or joining the Defense/Paramilitary forces.
Role_1.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th (Physical Education as an elective is a huge plus). Pursue a BPED (Bachelor of Physical Education) or a B.Sc in Sports Science. Complete professional fitness certifications like ACE or specialized strength and conditioning courses.

Role_2.title: Performance / Video Analyst
Role_2.primary_match_text: You have a super analytical brain! You know that sports aren't just played on the field; they are won in the mind. You love finding patterns, tracking stats, and outsmarting the opponent.
Role_2.day_in_the_life: Sitting with a laptop and specialized sports software, watching match replays, finding the weak spots of rival teams, and presenting crucial data to the head coach before a big final.
Role_2.alternative_match_text: Your love for data and patterns also makes you highly suited for Data Analytics, Esports Coaching, or being a Sports Statistician.
Role_2.roadmap: Take Science (PCM) or Commerce with Math in 11th/12th. Pursue a degree in Data Analytics, Statistics, or a B.Sc in Sports Science. You can then do specialized diploma courses in Sports Analytics (offered by various Indian sports management institutes).

Role_3.title: Technique & Form Expert
Role_3.primary_match_text: You have an eagle eye for detail! You understand the human body like a machine. You can watch a player for 5 seconds and instantly know exactly what tiny change will make their performance 10x better.
Role_3.day_in_the_life: Recording players with slow-motion cameras, fixing a batsman's stance, correcting a bowler's wrist position, and ensuring athletes don't get injured due to bad posture.
Role_3.alternative_match_text: Your deep understanding of body mechanics makes you an amazing Sports Physiotherapist, Biomechanist, or Yoga/Martial Arts Instructor.
Role_3.roadmap: Opt for Science (PCB) in 11th/12th. Pursue a Bachelor of Physiotherapy (BPT), B.Sc in Sports Science, or Biomechanics. Working alongside sports academies to fix player forms will be your primary career launchpad.

Role_4.title: Head Coach / Selector
Role_4.primary_match_text: You are the ultimate leader! You look at the big picture. You know how to manage egos, unite a team, handle immense pressure, and make the tough decisions that win championships.
Role_4.day_in_the_life: Selecting the playing 11, designing master match strategies, motivating players with powerful speeches, and handling the media after a massive victory (or defeat).
Role_4.alternative_match_text: Your leadership and strategy skills translate perfectly to Sports Management, Entrepreneurship, or Corporate Leadership Roles.
Role_4.roadmap: Take any stream in 11th/12th. Pursue a BPED, BA, or BBA. The ultimate gold standard for coaching in India is completing the NSNIS (Netaji Subhas National Institute of Sports) Diploma in Sports Coaching. Having a strong background as a former state/national level player helps immensely.
